sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems designed to understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of neural network called transformers and are trained on vast amounts of text data. This training helps them learn the relationships between words and phrases.

sections.title: How LLMs Process Text
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are then transformed into embeddings, which are numerical representations that capture the meaning of the text. This process allows LLMs to predict what comes next in a sentence accurately.

sections.title: The Role of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or instructions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. The way we phrase these prompts can greatly influence the quality of the answers we receive. By carefully designing prompts, we can improve the relevance and accuracy of the LLM's output.

sections.title: Enhancing LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering and automatic prompt generation help customize how LLMs respond. For example, Chain-of-Thought prompting encourages the model to show its reasoning step-by-step, which can lead to better answers, especially for complex questions. These methods aim to reduce errors and improve the reliability of the information provided.
